rationale: Round 3 at a8ac1fc4. My round-2 hard_block required one of two dispositions: (a) close the bd-capable-actor forgery gap for real via signature verification, or (b) state the trust boundary honestly (narrows-not-closes, local-operator-environment trust made explicit, no 'closes' framing) and file a tracked follow-up citing its ID. The fix commit delivers (b), and I re-derived every element of it rather than trusting the summary. Read the actual new ADR-0041 paragraph (SS 'Honest trust boundary (final-review round 2, R12)', inserted after the attestation paragraph): it states plainly 'the attestation NARROWS the forgery, it does not close it', names the exact mechanism (bd metadata is writable with ordinary bd CLI access, which every implementer agent holds by design), states precisely what it DOES buy (git-only forgery dead, a durable attributable tracker write forced, the premise reframed honestly as 'the local operator environment's bd store corroborates the publication'), and explicitly disclaims adversarial-integrity framing ('it is not an adversarial-integrity control against a bd-capable actor'). Read the matching doc-comment edits in internal/complete/materialize.go: stageMarkerAttestationKey's comment carries the identical 'HONEST TRUST BOUNDARY' block, and the PROVENANCE paragraph on resolveMaterializationDiscriminator was reworded from 'the executed forgery this closes' to 'the executed forgery this NARROWS' with the same bd-capable-actor caveat and 'nothing resumes on evidence the local bd store does not corroborate' (no longer implying cryptographic proof). Grepped every other doc site that mentions the attestation (merge-safety.md, execution/architecture.md, workflow/architecture.md, workflow/runbook.md) for lingering 'closes'/'proves'/'prevents' framing — none found; execution/architecture.md's one mention is a neutral mechanism description ('required to match at resume'), consistent with the new honest framing, not contradicting it. Verified the cited follow-up is real, not just prose: `bd show mindspec-an8q` returns an OPEN P2 task whose title accurately states the escalation ('verify the write-ahead marker commit's signature against an operator-trusted key... when CommitSigningEnabled... escalation of spec-128's bd-attestation which narrows but does not close marker forgery against a bd-capable actor. From spec-128 final review R12 round 2') — correctly attributed and technically accurate to what I found. This satisfies my bar: the finding is no longer at risk of being silently described as closed, the residual capability gap is disclosed at both the decision (ADR) and implementation (doc-comment) layers in the same words, and there is a real, tracked, correctly-scoped path to actually closing it. Spot-checked the round-3 diff's one other complete-package change relevant to my lens (mergeMetadataEscaped/getMetadataEscaped, complete.go:169-193, R2's finding) — clean thin wrappers routing through the already-verified next.RenderBDError escape discipline, Unwrap preserved, no new operand or argv site. Nothing in this round's 8-file diff disturbs my round-1/round-2 basis. My residual is ADDRESSED via disposition (b); no outstanding ask from me.

findings.title: R12 round-2 disposition (b) verified delivered and accurate
findings.detail: ADR-0041's 'Honest trust boundary (final-review round 2, R12)' paragraph and the matching internal/complete/materialize.go doc comments (stageMarkerAttestationKey, resolveMaterializationDiscriminator's PROVENANCE paragraph) now state plainly that the bd-metadata attestation narrows the round-1 git-only forgery but does not close it against an actor with ordinary bd CLI access (every implementer agent, by design) — no residual 'closes'/'proves' language anywhere I could find. The signature-verification escalation that would actually close the gap (attested AND marker-commit signature verified against an operator-trusted key when signing is enabled) is tracked as bd issue mindspec-an8q, confirmed real and correctly titled via `bd show`. This is the accepted, honestly-disclosed disposition of my round-2 hard_block finding; the underlying capability gap remains open by design pending mindspec-an8q, not silently closed.
